_doc: Revert-verify mutants for #4264 (req cb707868-356f-495d-825a-182e66ba8bcd) on the MULTI-PROCESS harness (three spawned `dist/index.js` processes; the harness rebuilds the copy's dist first, ~1 s). Subject packages/cli/src/cache/CacheManager.ts. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py packages/cli/tests/integration/use-cache-4264.proc-chain.cachemanager.spec.json after setting `tree` and `subject` (both absolute). Local only — CI has no built CLI; the in-process chain is CI axis A4. ⛔ Precondition — `npm run build` at the WORKSPACE ROOT first, not just `npm run build -w @kitelev/exocortex-cli`: `npm ci` builds neither `packages/core/dist` nor `packages/services/dist`, and `packages/cli/esbuild.config.mjs` resolves both workspace deps through their package `main` (= `dist/index.js`), so on a freshly installed tree the harness's own CLI rebuild cannot resolve them and it exits before a single axis runs. The driver then reports a green control and `красные = НИ ОДНОЙ` for every mutant — which reads exactly like "no mutant discriminates" (#4471; as of 2026-09-29 `mutant-driver.py` prints the control's rc beside the red count, so that false picture is flagged rather than silent).

PM1_write_through_is_a_noop_(next_proces.to: const base = null as CacheData | null; void this.loadedIsCurrent;
PM1_write_through_is_a_noop_(next_proces._note: Measured 2026-09-29 (#4471). P2: `refreshAfterWrite` has no base, so it returns `skipped` and the notice reads `write-through skipped (no cache to refresh)`. P3/P4: nothing was folded, so each next process pays `delta (1 file(s) re-parsed)` where `hit` is asserted. P8 is NOT chain propagation but a second call site of the same subject: `CacheManager.refreshAfterWrite` is the single implementation behind EVERY write-through, `create --write-through` included, so `c1` reports the same `skipped` notice and `c2` then pays a `delta` for c1's file instead of the asserted hit — the old `expect` enumerated only the `apply` chain. P7 IS the downstream one: it pays the delta P4 left un-folded (`stdout identical=true`). P9 stays GREEN because it asserts the no-write-through default, and that path never calls `refreshAfterWrite`.

PM2_restamp_without_reparse_(stale_preco._note: Measured 2026-09-29 (#4471). The mutant re-stamps a changed file's cache entry with ZERO triples, so every later reader gets an honest `hit` on stamps and an empty entry on content. P3: process 2's stderr (probed directly, the harness only surfaces rc) is `"<created>" contributed no triples, so preconditions and $target reads see nothing` followed by `❌ "Move to Backlog (4264)" is not bound to the target's class`, rc=5 `OPERATION_FAILED`. ⚠ `refused(p2)` is FALSE — this axis catches the stale hit through `p2.status === 0`, NOT through its "Precondition not satisfied" conjunct. P2 stays GREEN: it only checks the notice text (`persisted (1 file(s) re-parsed)` is truthful — the re-parse DID run, it just stored nothing) and that the file exists, so the first CONSUMER is the earliest axis able to see this at all. P4 is chain PROPAGATION, not a second direct hit — this was challenged and corrected in review of PR #4474, and the distinction is mechanical: p2's grounding is rejected before it writes, so the created file's mtime/size never change again; `diffManifest` compares stamps ONLY, reports an empty diff, and process 3 takes the HIT branch (`CacheManager.ts:453-463`) that returns BEFORE `applyDelta`, so the mutated `makeEntry` runs ZERO times inside p3. Measured: `load=[⚡ triple cache: hit]`, p3 fails rc=5 on the entry p1 mis-wrote, `doing=false` because the flip never happened. P5: the cached vault therefore never received flips 2 and 3, so its final file differs from the no-flag twin (`file identical=false`; the stdout envelopes still match). P7: the #3788 stale hit reaching a READER — `load=[hit]` but `stdout identical=false`, because `resolve-buttons` resolves against a store where the target has no class and no status and so offers a different button set than the twin. P9 is NOT propagation from P3/P4 but the same mutation on the other consumer of `makeEntry`: the delta path runs the same `applyDelta` → `makeEntry`, so `d2`'s fresh entry for `created2` is stamped empty as well and `d2` fails rc=5. The discriminator against P4 above is measured, not argued: `d2 load=[♻️ triple cache: delta (1 file(s) re-parsed)]` — a delta REACHES `applyDelta`, a hit does not. P8 stays GREEN because `c2` is `create --dry-run --validate`, which never reads the created file's triples.
